fixer.summary: Selling now has one value mechanism. I added `Item.sale_price()` in `dungdra/items.py`: if the item has a `sell_value` prop, that is the price of one unit; otherwise it is half of `listed_cost()`, rounded down, and an unpriced item is refused. `gear.sell()` now just calls `it.sale_price() * qty`, so the override that ran after the price was computed is gone. I removed the old module-level `sale_price()` function and its docstring, which wrongly said trade goods keep full value. In `tests/unit/test_items.py` the existing tests now call the new method, and one new test checks that `sell_value` replaces the half price, even on an item with no listed cost. Unit tests, the full test suite (599 passed), ruff and dev-gate all pass. The ticket names no acceptance tests, so there was nothing to run with `--runxfail`. One thing I left alone: `sell()`'s log message still says "(half price)", even when `sell_value` sets a different price.

review.summary:
Approved: the change does what T-35 asks and I found no problems. Selling now has one value mechanism. The module-level `sale_price` function is replaced by `Item.sale_price()`, which returns the `sell_value` prop when it is set and otherwise half of `listed_cost()` (rounded down). It still refuses an item with no price. `sell()` in `dungdra/gear.py` just calls `it.sale_price() * qty` and no longer applies its own override afterwards. The wrong docstring is fixed too: it no longer says trade goods keep full value, and it describes `sell_value` as the override.

One behaviour change: before, an item with `sell_value` but no listed cost was refused, because the half-price calculation ran before the override. Now it sells at its `sell_value`. That follows from the single mechanism the ticket asks for, and a new unit test asserts it.

No other callers of the old function were left behind. The tests check outcomes: the halving, rounding down, the refusal, and `sell_value` taking precedence. The existing gear test `test_sell_value_prop_still_overrides_the_sale_price` still covers the full sell path. The diff also touches `loop/costs.jsonl`, but that is only the loop's own cost log. All gates pass.
